english.note: This is the all-purpose choice for physical discomfort, whether a thing causes it or a person feels it.

exampleSentences.traditional: 我今日個肚有啲唔舒服。
exampleSentences.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 jat6 go3 tou5 jau5 di1 m4 syu1 fuk6

english.note: This is the all-purpose choice for saying that you are not feeling well.

exampleSentences.english: I feel unwell today and want to take half a day off.
exampleSentences.traditional: 我今日有啲唔舒服，想請半日假。
exampleSentences.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 jat6 jau5 di1 m4 syu1 fuk6 soeng2 cing2 bun3 jat6 gaa3

english.note: Use this for generally feeling unwell, including feeling rough after drinking, though it does not specifically state that the cause is a hangover.

exampleSentences.english: I drank too much last night, and I feel seedy today.
exampleSentences.traditional: 我琴晚飲多咗，今日成身都唔舒服。
exampleSentences.jyutping: ngo5 kam4 maan5 jam2 do1 zo2 gam1 jat6 seng4 san1 dou1 m4 syu1 fuk6

english.note: Use 唔舒服 when upset means feeling physically unwell, nauseated, or ready to vomit.

exampleSentences.english: My stomach feels upset, and I feel like vomiting.
exampleSentences.jyutping: ngo5 go3 wai6 hou2 m4 syu1 fuk6 soeng2 au2

english.note: Use this when “lousy” means that someone feels physically unwell or under the weather.

exampleSentences.english: I feel lousy today and don’t want to go out.
exampleSentences.traditional: 我今日個人唔舒服，唔想出街。
exampleSentences.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 jat6 go3 jan4 m4 syu1 fuk6 m4 soeng2 ceot1 gaai1

english.note: Use this when something causes physical or emotional discomfort.

exampleSentences.english: After sitting in a car for so long, my stomach feels uneasy.
exampleSentences.traditional: 坐咁耐車，我個胃有啲唔舒服。
exampleSentences.jyutping: co5 gam3 noi6 ce1 ngo5 go3 wai6 jau5 di1 m4 syu1 fuk6
